data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 explains the §11.3 flag as a benign artifact of temporal misalignment ('snapshot divergence') and asserts the flag is sustained only by a bookkeeping failure, not by any deep structural reason. But the problem standard asks the target to *audit the critic* under §11.3 — i.e., determine whether the flag is legitimately sustained. SRC_001 instead explains the flag away as a bookkeeping artifact without establishing that the underlying affirmations and failures were actually computed at different rounds against different claim versions. The target's core diagnosis ('verdicts that were never co-temporal') is asserted without evidence: no commitment or quoted material ties any cited source (SRC_006–SRC_009) to distinct evaluation rounds or distinct claim versions. If in fact the verdicts were co-temporal against the same claim version, the entire 'snapshot divergence' explanation collapses and the flag reflects a genuine structural contradiction rather than a bookkeeping artifact. The target fails the audit standard because it substitutes an unsupported causal hypothesis for the required adjudication of whether the §11.3 flag is genuinely sustained.
